[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This facility, Tahoe Reno 3, is part of Switchs Citadel Campus (Tahoe Reno) in Storey County, Nevada. Per Switchs own press release announcing the Tahoe Reno campus opening (tier-1 operator source, https://www.switch.com/switch-tahoe-reno-data-center-now-open/), this is the Citadel Campus, a 2,000 acre site in the Tahoe Reno Industrial Center in Storey County, Nevada, next to the Tesla Gigafactory, designed for up to 7.2 million square feet and up to 650 MW of power at full build out, a small fraction of which this registry currently tracks as five buildings. Aggregator directories (datacenterHawk, DataCenterMap) give 1 Superloop Circle, Reno, NV as the address for this campus, the same address appears attached to more than one individually numbered Tahoe Reno building on these directories, so it is treated here as a shared campus level address rather than a distinct address for any one building. Switch own official locations page (fetched directly this session, https://www.switch.com/locations/) names five exascale campuses, the Citadel in Tahoe Reno, the Pyramid Campus in Grand Rapids, the Core Campus in Las Vegas, the Keep Campus in Atlanta, and the Rock Campus in Austin and Houston, but confirms no street address for any campus or building, directing visitors to a contact form instead. This registry rows address, where given below, therefore comes from data center industry aggregator directories, leads-only sources per this projects source hierarchy, not confirmed directly by the operator. This buildings own datacenterHawk listing independently repeats the same 1 Superloop Circle address.

reading.body:
Tahoe Reno 3 is one building on the Citadel Campus, a 2,000 acre site in Storey County designed for up to 650 MW at full buildout across multiple structures, though this registry currently tracks only five of those buildings. The operator has not published power or floor space figures specific to this building alone. Nevada has published capacity figures from only two facilities totaling 10.37 MW, making statewide capacity data sparse, so Tahoe Reno's rank by published figures reflects the absence of data from other operators as much as the site's actual scale.

The Citadel Campus sits adjacent to Tesla's Gigafactory in an industrial zone positioned for hyperscale compute. At full build, 650 MW would support roughly 16,000 racks at 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density. The campus location in Nevada gives access to the state's power resources, though the specific grid connection terms and available capacity are not published.

What this campus means for AI depends on build pace and tenant mix, neither published here. The operator runs exascale campuses and has positioned Citadel for scale, but until individual buildings report their own power allocations or tenancy, the strategic significance remains a function of the operator's capital spending and the grid's willingness to serve it.
